highlights.title: NeurIPS Poster TSNBench: Benchmarking LLM Proficiency in Time-Sensitive Networking
highlights.titleZh: NeurIPS Poster TSNBench: Benchmarking LLM Proficiency in Time-Sensitive Networking
highlights.content: # TSNBench: Benchmarking LLM Proficiency in Time-Sensitive Networking ### Abstract We present TSNBench, the first benchmark for evaluating large language model (LLM) proficiency in Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN), a suite of IEEE 802.1 standards for deterministic communication with bounded latency in safety-critical domains such as autonomous vehicles, aviation, defense, and industrial automation. While LLMs have been extensively evaluated on general knowledge tasks, their capabilities in safety-critical networking domains remain largely unexplored. TSNBench comprises 939 expert-validated multiple-choice questions (MCQs) covering diverse TSN mechanisms, along with 100 open-ended Worst-Case Delay (WCD) computation tasks for Credit-Based Shaper (CBS) and Cyclic Queuing and Forwarding (CQF) across varying network topologies and traffic conditions. MCQ answers are validated by domain experts, and open-ended ground truth WCD values are computed using a verified Network Calculus (NC) solver for CBS and closed-form mathematical upper bounds for CQF. We evaluate 16 LLMs and find that although models achieve 67 to 95\\% accuracy on MCQs, they fail substantially on open-ended WCD computation. For CBS, only GPT-5 achieves a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 36.2\\%, meaning its predicted WCD deviates by 36.2\\% of the actual TSN flow delay on average, while most models exceed 80\\%. For CQF, the best model achieves 41.8\\% MAPE, with most models clustering between 80\\% and 100\\%. Such errors are large relative to TSN latency budgets and can lead to violations of real-time constraints and unsafe configurations. TSNBench demonstrates that MCQ benchmarks may overestimate LLM capabilities in safety-critical networking domains.

highlights.content: # Beyond the Hype: 6 Mind-Bending Takeaways About the Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol ## Introduction: The Agent Tower of Babel The artificial intelligence landscape is experiencing an unprecedented surge in autonomous AI agents. Developers and enterprise engineering teams are building specialized agents across a fragmented web of frameworks — ranging from LangGraph, CrewAI, and Semantic Kernel to Google’s Agent Development Kit (ADK) and custom in-house codebases. While these agents excel at executing local decisions, perceiving isolated environments, and performing task-specific actions, a critical architectural bottleneck has emerged: how do independent AI agents communicate and delegate tasks without requiring custom, point-to-point glue code for every single integration? Consider a complex workflow like automated travel management. Fulfilling an end-user request requires an overarching trip planner agent to coordinate with a flight booking agent, a hotel reservation agent, and a local excursion agent. If every agent framework relies on proprietary communication interfaces, building cross-system workflows becomes prohibitively expensive, fragile, and unscalable. Swapping out a hotel agent for a third-party vendor’s alternative requires re-engineering custom API integrations from scratch. This interoperability challenge — the “Agent Tower of Babel” — is precisely what the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol solves. Initially introduced by Google in April 2025 and now housed under neutral governance by the Linux Foundation within the Agentic AI Foundation under an Apache 2.0 open-source license, A2A provides an open, universal standard. It serves as a common language for opaque agentic applications to dynamically discover one another, negotiate security capabilities, delegate sub-tasks, stream rich media, and orchestrate complex multi-agent workflows across enterprise boundaries. ## 1: A2A and MCP Are Teammates, Not Rivals A persistent misconception in the developer community is that the Agent2Agent protocol competes directly with Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP). In reality, A2A and MCP address two entirely distinct layers of the modern agentic stack, operating as complementary teammates rather than rivals. - **MCP (Model Context Protocol):** Operates at the agent-to-resource layer. It standardizes how an individual agent connects to its local tools, external APIs, databases, and context repositories — effectively standardizing function calling and tool execution. - **A2A (Agent2Agent Protocol):** Operates at the agent-to-agent layer. It standardizes peer-to-peer interaction between independent agents, enabling them to discover capabilities, delegate complex multi-step tasks, and negotiate multi-turn workflows across distinct system boundaries. In a sophisticated agentic architecture, agents rely on MCP to interact with their underlying tools and database engines, while using A2A to discover, negotiate, and delegate tasks to peer agents across enterprise ecosystems. “MCP is all about how an agent connects to its tools, APIs, and resources… A2A, on the other hand, facilitates dynamic communication between different independent agents acting as peers… So you’ll often see both in a sophisticated agentic system. Agents use A2A to coordinate with other agents, and they use MCP to interact with their tools to get part of the job done.” — Holt Skinner, Developer Advocate, Google Cloud AI ## 2: Opacity is a Security Feature, Not a Bug Early multi-agent research frameworks often relied on open-state architectures, where collaborating agents shared full prompt histories, joint memory stores, or raw vector contexts. While this works in isolated sandbox experiments, sharing internal states across organizational boundaries in enterprise B2B environments is an absolute non-starter. In one, threat actors used AI agents to harvest API keys and other credentials, feeding them back into the framework to sustain further searches for access to large language models. Targets included gateways and platforms such as One API, LiteLLM, Dify and Open WebUI. ***AWS Chief Information Security Officer [CJ Moses](https://www.linkedin.com/in/cjmoses/) noted that agents validated identities, enumerated storage and pursued secrets across managed AI services.*** A second campaign generated real-time deepfake videos to spoof know-your-customer checks at cryptocurrency exchanges, while also forging document metadata. FBI warns hackers weaponizing ARTEX AI framework to automate attacks on energy, manufacturing, telecom November 17, 2026 ![FBI warns hackers weaponizing ARTEX AI framework to automate attacks on energy, manufacturing, telecom](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='https://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%201200%20628'%3E%3C/svg%3E) The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) warned in a FLASH advisory that hackers are using ARTEX, an open-source, large language model (LLM)-driven autonomous penetration testing framework, to automate multiple stages of cyber intrusions, from reconnaissance and initial access to privilege escalation and data exfiltration. Photo: Penguin Random House Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman tells Axios the software giant is making significant progress toward building its own frontier general-purpose AI model, even as it introduces six specialized models that it claims rival leading offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic at a fraction of the cost. Why it matters: Microsoft has long relied on OpenAI and other AI companies for its most advanced models. Now it's demonstrating that it can develop competitive technology of its own, and the new offerings show how aggressively the tech giant plans to compete on price. Driving the news: Microsoft is announcing six new AI models Tuesday at its Ignite conference in San Francisco. The models span coding, cybersecurity, image generation and voice. OpenAI is releasing new models, including Astra and Sol 6.2, which Between the lines: Microsoft's strategy is to build models specialized for particular tasks, allowing them to achieve comparable performance at significantly lower costs. "It basically means that you cram more tokens and knowledge and expertise into the same amount of parameters," Suleyman told Axios. The big picture: Even as Microsoft targets the industry's leaders, frontier AI keeps moving forward as well. OpenAI on Tuesday announced GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol, with the new Astra priced 20 percent less than the prior version. The intrigue: The new models could reshape Microsoft's relationship with OpenAI and other outside AI providers. Zoom in: Microsoft is also offering enterprise customers access to licensed model weights, allowing them to customize its models with proprietary data while requiring deployment within Azure. What to watch: How quickly Microsoft can translate its progress in specialized AI into a competitive general-purpose model — and whether its cost advantages are enough to persuade customers to switch from established rivals.

AI Agents.content: # Beyond the Hype: 6 Mind-Bending Takeaways About the Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol ## Introduction: The Agent Tower of Babel The artificial intelligence landscape is experiencing an unprecedented surge in autonomous AI agents. Developers and enterprise engineering teams are building specialized agents across a fragmented web of frameworks — ranging from LangGraph, CrewAI, and Semantic Kernel to Google’s Agent Development Kit (ADK) and custom in-house codebases. While these agents excel at executing local decisions, perceiving isolated environments, and performing task-specific actions, a critical architectural bottleneck has emerged: how do independent AI agents communicate and delegate tasks without requiring custom, point-to-point glue code for every single integration? Consider a complex workflow like automated travel management. Fulfilling an end-user request requires an overarching trip planner agent to coordinate with a flight booking agent, a hotel reservation agent, and a local excursion agent. If every agent framework relies on proprietary communication interfaces, building cross-system workflows becomes prohibitively expensive, fragile, and unscalable. Swapping out a hotel agent for a third-party vendor’s alternative requires re-engineering custom API integrations from scratch. This interoperability challenge — the “Agent Tower of Babel” — is precisely what the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol solves. Initially introduced by Google in April 2025 and now housed under neutral governance by the Linux Foundation within the Agentic AI Foundation under an Apache 2.0 open-source license, A2A provides an open, universal standard. It serves as a common language for opaque agentic applications to dynamically discover one another, negotiate security capabilities, delegate sub-tasks, stream rich media, and orchestrate complex multi-agent workflows across enterprise boundaries. ## 1: A2A and MCP Are Teammates, Not Rivals A persistent misconception in the developer community is that the Agent2Agent protocol competes directly with Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP). In reality, A2A and MCP address two entirely distinct layers of the modern agentic stack, operating as complementary teammates rather than rivals. - **MCP (Model Context Protocol):** Operates at the agent-to-resource layer. It standardizes how an individual agent connects to its local tools, external APIs, databases, and context repositories — effectively standardizing function calling and tool execution. - **A2A (Agent2Agent Protocol):** Operates at the agent-to-agent layer. It standardizes peer-to-peer interaction between independent agents, enabling them to discover capabilities, delegate complex multi-step tasks, and negotiate multi-turn workflows across distinct system boundaries. In a sophisticated agentic architecture, agents rely on MCP to interact with their underlying tools and database engines, while using A2A to discover, negotiate, and delegate tasks to peer agents across enterprise ecosystems. “MCP is all about how an agent connects to its tools, APIs, and resources… A2A, on the other hand, facilitates dynamic communication between different independent agents acting as peers… So you’ll often see both in a sophisticated agentic system. Agents use A2A to coordinate with other agents, and they use MCP to interact with their tools to get part of the job done.” — Holt Skinner, Developer Advocate, Google Cloud AI ## 2: Opacity is a Security Feature, Not a Bug Early multi-agent research frameworks often relied on open-state architectures, where collaborating agents shared full prompt histories, joint memory stores, or raw vector contexts. While this works in isolated sandbox experiments, sharing internal states across organizational boundaries in enterprise B2B environments is an absolute non-starter. AI Agents Automate Cyber Attacks On Critical Sectors Uploaded on 2026-11-17 in [TECHNOLOGY-Key Areas-Artificial Intelligence](https://www.cybersecurityintelligence.com/blog/category/technology-key-areas-artificial-intelligence-36.html "TECHNOLOGY-Key Areas-Artificial Intelligence"), [TECHNOLOGY--Hackers](https://www.cybersecurityintelligence.com/blog/category/technology--hackers-17.html "TECHNOLOGY--Hackers"), [GOVERNMENT-Law Enforcement](https://www.cybersecurityintelligence.com/blog/category/government-law-enforcement-14.html "GOVERNMENT-Law Enforcement"), [FREE TO VIEW](https://www.cybersecurityintelligence.com/blog/category/free-to-view-25.html "FREE TO VIEW") ***![](https://www.cybersecurityintelligence.com/files/upload/htmleditor/security-alert-text-replacement%20ideogram.jpg)Cybercriminals are deploying an open-source AI penetration testing framework to automate attacks on banks, governments, energy providers, healthcare organisations and other critical sectors worldwide.*** ***Security alerts from the FBI and Amazon Threat Intelligence, issued in mid-November 2026, highlight how the tool known as [ARTEX enables rapid, multi-stage intrusions](https://www.cybersecurityintelligence.com/blog/artex-ai-agents-weaponised-to-enable-automated-network-break-ins-9908.html) with minimal human oversight.*** ***These campaigns have already facilitated the theft of AI model credentials and the creation of deepfake videos designed to bypass identity checks.*** Amazon’s **[MadPot honeypot sensors](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/amazon-madpot-stops-cybersecurity-crime)** detected two distinct ARTEX campaigns between early October and early November. There is a clear need for autonomous analytical solutions that can utilize recent advancements in agentic AI such as agent harnessing and loop engineering without introducing hallucination or workflow fragmentation. Researchers, regardless of technical expertise, need tools that streamline complex data analysis and deliver meaningful, actionable insights grounded in both data and established biomedical knowledge. EcoXAI addresses this by introducing a modular, customizable, containerized multi-agent system that structures analysis into explicit pipeline execution stages, lowering the computational barrier for clinical and translational researchers. Result: EcoXAI replaces monolithic AI text interfaces with an autonomous execution-driven framework with specialized bioinformatics agents for delivering proactive, data-driven insights grounded in established biological knowledge. Unlike purely LLM-driven or less integrated AI solutions prone to hallucinations or biologically implausible outcomes, EcoXAI’s multi-agent framework, which leverages modern agentic management and explicit knowledge graph integration, provides greater transparency and verifiability in its reasoning. In our use case in drug repurposing for Alzheimer’s Disease, EcoXAI evaluated 103 drug candidates and identified 79 novel candidates whose predictive models exceeded a randomized baseline, including the CCR5 antagonist Maraviroc, whose generated hypothesis was subsequently supported by the literature. These results demonstrate the potential of knowledge graph-grounded AI agents to accelerate hypothesis-driven biomedical research. AI Agents.title: JPMorgan is working on AI agent transactions that don’t involve humans
AI Agents.titleZh: JPMorgan is working on AI agent transactions that don’t involve humans
AI Agents.content: Artificial intelligence agents have already proven to be helpful, or cause a lot of trouble, or both. One area seen as high-potential is in payments, where — if they're able to be trusted — the agents could deal with all sorts of money matters on behalf of people. That's why JPMorgan Chase and South Korea's Hyundai Card are testing how AI agents can handle financial transactions without direct human intervention, including whether they can eventually negotiate and make payments with one another. The companies have completed an initial proof-of-concept involving a simulated foreign exchange transaction and are targeting the first half of 2027 for a more complex phase involving multiple AI agents. > What happens when agents are negotiating, agreeing directly with each other and then making payments? What does that actually look like?Wee Kee TohGlobal Head, Kinexys Insights Wee Kee Toh, global head of Kinexys Insights at Kinexys by JP Morgan, told CNBC that the next step is to test what happens when autonomous agents move beyond execution and begin interacting with each other in an ecosystem. "That, I would say, is really the biggest part of what we want to get as an expansion of the phase one scope," he added. The initial trial involved a Hyundai Card AI agent requesting a foreign exchange transaction to maintain euro liquidity in its Kinexys blockchain deposit account. JPMorgan said it was the first private blockchain-based autonomous bank-agent-to-client-agent test for corporate treasury management. ## Beyond the pilot While the initial trial has been completed, JPMorgan has yet to set a timeline for commercializing the technology. Toh said building the technology itself was relatively straightforward, but establishing appropriate governance and internal controls proved more difficult. "Technology-wise, it's really not the biggest hurdle," he said, pointing instead to questions around accountability and the risks of allowing AI agents to execute financial transactions without direct human oversight. To address those concerns, Kinexys developed a framework that restricts AI agents to predefined transaction parameters, automatically rejecting requests that fall outside authorized limits. "You are going to draw a box around the agent. The agent will never be able to do anything out of the box," Toh said. For example, an AI agent authorized to transact up to $5 million would be blocked from executing transactions above that threshold, he said. The companies are also exploring whether to extend their collaboration to other businesses within Hyundai Motor Group, whose broader operations were one reason JPMorgan selected Hyundai Card as a partner, Toh said. No specific projects have been announced. Hyundai Motor Group holds a combined 78.04% stake in Hyundai Card through Hyundai Motor, Kia and Hyundai Commercial, according to the card issuer's website. Hyundai Card has previously experimented with blockchain-based cross-border payments. In July, the company said it completed a proof-of-concept involving a $20,000 transfer using the USDT stablecoin between Hyundai Motor's U.S. and Mexican subsidiaries, with the transfer and verification process taking an average of seven minutes. Kinexys has also been expanding its blockchain-based payments business. The JPMorgan unit said in August that it had processed more than $4 trillion in transactions since inception, averaging about $7 billion a day. Separately, JPMorgan launched a proof-of-concept for its dollar-denominated deposit token, JPMD, in June 2025, before making it available to institutional clients that November.

AI Agents.title: Google Buys AI Scheduling Tool Howie in Latest Agents Push
AI Agents.titleZh: Google Buys AI Scheduling Tool Howie in Latest Agents Push
AI Agents.content: (Bloomberg) -- Alphabet Inc.'s Google has bought Howie, an artificial intelligence-powered scheduling and calendar management tool, the tech giant's latest move to win over consumers with AI agents. Most Read from Bloomberg Google's experimental arm, Google Labs, announced the purchase Monday in an X post, without disclosing terms. Howie, whose tool lets users loop the AI agent into emails as they would a human secretary, was valued at $14 million in 2024, according to PitchBook data. "We can't wait to learn from them as we build the next generation of intuitive AI tools together for small businesses," Google Labs said in the post. Tech and AI companies have been intensely focused on developing AI agents that can do things on behalf of the user, an advancement beyond question-and-answer chatbots. In May, Google released Gemini Spark, a 24/7 agent that proactively completes digital tasks such as scan an inbox for emails, organize files or build a spreadsheet. That market is growing increasingly crowded, with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic PBC, Meta Platforms Inc. and Elon Musk's xAI. Austin Petersmith, Howie's co-founder and chief executive officer, said his team will "continue building" the tool at Google. "Howie has always been built on top of Gmail and Google Calendar, so Google Labs is the perfect place for us to take this product to the next level," he said Monday in a LinkedIn post. Petersmith and Google Labs did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the deal terms, or whether Howie will eventually be integrated into Google apps and services. Google Labs has previously acquired AI tools built on Google technology. In February, it bought ProducerAI, a music generation platform that uses Google DeepMind's Lyria model. LLMs.title: NeurIPS Poster TSNBench: Benchmarking LLM Proficiency in Time-Sensitive Networking
LLMs.titleZh: NeurIPS Poster TSNBench: Benchmarking LLM Proficiency in Time-Sensitive Networking
LLMs.content: # TSNBench: Benchmarking LLM Proficiency in Time-Sensitive Networking ### Abstract We present TSNBench, the first benchmark for evaluating large language model (LLM) proficiency in Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN), a suite of IEEE 802.1 standards for deterministic communication with bounded latency in safety-critical domains such as autonomous vehicles, aviation, defense, and industrial automation. While LLMs have been extensively evaluated on general knowledge tasks, their capabilities in safety-critical networking domains remain largely unexplored. TSNBench comprises 939 expert-validated multiple-choice questions (MCQs) covering diverse TSN mechanisms, along with 100 open-ended Worst-Case Delay (WCD) computation tasks for Credit-Based Shaper (CBS) and Cyclic Queuing and Forwarding (CQF) across varying network topologies and traffic conditions. MCQ answers are validated by domain experts, and open-ended ground truth WCD values are computed using a verified Network Calculus (NC) solver for CBS and closed-form mathematical upper bounds for CQF. We evaluate 16 LLMs and find that although models achieve 67 to 95\\% accuracy on MCQs, they fail substantially on open-ended WCD computation. For CBS, only GPT-5 achieves a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 36.2\\%, meaning its predicted WCD deviates by 36.2\\% of the actual TSN flow delay on average, while most models exceed 80\\%. For CQF, the best model achieves 41.8\\% MAPE, with most models clustering between 80\\% and 100\\%. Such errors are large relative to TSN latency budgets and can lead to violations of real-time constraints and unsafe configurations. TSNBench demonstrates that MCQ benchmarks may overestimate LLM capabilities in safety-critical networking domains.

Describe the issue below: ![archive](https://static.arxiv.org/static/design-system/latest/logos/arxiv-logo.svg) # ANCHOR: Cluster-Grounded 5W1H Extraction via Large-Small Model Collaboration ###### Abstract Deep semantic understanding of events requires recognizing related events and distinguishing why an event occurs from how it is carried out. 5W1H extraction provides a structured foundation for such understanding by organizing event information around six fundamental questions. However, single-event slot filling provides limited support for these distinctions. We propose Anchor, a cluster-grounded framework that combines a large language model (LLM) with a small language model equipped with discriminative heads for accurate 5W1H extraction. The LLM proposes candidate events and generates their initial 4W records, which guide the selection of an event cluster and the subsequent anchoring of its main event. A shared document encoder provides evidence for joint 4W refinement, and two separate sets of boundary and role-scoring heads then extract why and how under event-specific constraints, respectively. Document representations are reused across events and stages, and unsupported roles can remain empty. Following the same principles, an agent-and-skill annotation workflow constructs a benchmark of 26,110 documents from ten source corpora covering three languages and seven domains. We select nine of the resulting datasets to evaluate Anchor against strong baselines using four open-weight LLMs. Anchor achieves competitive performance. The datasets and code are available at <https://github.com/revolution6575/ANCHOR-5W1H>. ###### Index Terms: ## I Introduction News articles, reports and online posts describe events in natural language. However, applications such as news aggregators, event knowledge graphs and monitoring dashboards require structured event records. Such records can also serve as structured evidence for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and reasoning about events and their relations. The 5W1H questions (who, when, where, what, why and how) go back to the circumstances of an action listed by Aristotle [[1](#bib.bib39)]. They break an event down into its participants, time, place, action, cause and means, and journalists answer them within the first few sentences of a story to report its main event [[2](#bib.bib1)]. They provide a compact schema for event records across domains and languages without requiring a manually constructed ontology. Therefore, extracting 5W1H information from text goes beyond language processing and constitutes a broader data engineering task. The information in a document’s event records must be consistent across events and traceable to the source, including any why and how evidence that may span multiple events. Methods for the task have moved from hand-written rules, as in Giveme5W1H [[3](#bib.bib2)], to large language models (LLMs) that are prompted [[4](#bib.bib38)] or fine-tuned [[5](#bib.bib41)] to answer the six questions. Along the way, who, when and where have generally become easier to extract, since their answers are often short spans, usually names, dates and places. What can likewise be extracted more readily using these three roles as context, whereas why and how often remain more challenging. Why and how were answered least precisely in the human evaluation of Giveme5W1H, while ChatGPT (GPT-3.5-turbo) [[6](#bib.bib40)] struggled most with what, why and how in the study by Cao et al. [[7](#bib.bib3)]. Five-shot LLMs evaluated on EVENT5Ws [[8](#bib.bib5)] achieve an exact-match F1 of up to 63.3 for when but no more than 11.3 for why, while how is absent from the benchmark’s annotations and evaluation. The new funding will allow Model ML to expand its research and engineering teams in London and New York to deepen product innovation and support broader customer deployments, per the release. Founded by brothers and serial entrepreneurs [Chaz Englander](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chazenglander/) and [Arnie Englander](https://uk.linkedin.com/in/arnie-englander), Model ML provides “every banker, consultant and investor their own personal AI agent,” according to the release. “The agent does not wait for instructions,” the release said. “It anticipates what matters, filters out the noise and executes. When news breaks on a company a banker covers, it does not simply send an alert. It judges whether the development matters, works through the implications and prepares the analysis in the firm’s own formats, in minutes rather than days. By the time the banker needs it, the work is already done.” Chaz Englander, who is also the startup’s CEO, downplayed the notion that the company’s chief purpose is to [reduce costs](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-17/ai-startup-for-bankers-raises-funds-at-1-5-billion-value), Bloomberg reported Tuesday. In situations like the breaking news story, the models can offer context and analysis of why the news matters. “The average age of a Model ML user is 33 years old, not 23 years old,” Chaz Englander said, per the report. “These tools are no longer productivity and efficiency tools. They’re revenue generative.” Small businesses showed more interest in using AI to keep track of their bills than in using it to pay them, according to the [PYMNTS Intelligence](https://www.pymnts.com/pymnts-intelligence/) report “[The Practical AI Opportunity: Why SMBs Want Guidance Before Automation](https://www.pymnts.com/report/tracker/the-practical-ai-opportunity-why-smbs-want-guidance-before-automation/),” published in June. It found that 31% of small- to medium-sized businesses (SMBs) wanted AI from their financial institution to monitor expenses and bills, while 22% wanted AI to help with budgeting, cash flow management, supplier discovery and financial product comparisons. Meanwhile, a November [Federal Reserve](https://www.federalreserve.gov/) survey showed banks are starting to consider how much access [AI agents](https://www.pymnts.com/news/banking/2026/banks-draw-lines-around-customers-ai-agents/) should have to customers’ online banking accounts amid growing security and account access concerns, PYMNTS reported Nov. 9. The survey of 70 bankers by the [Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas](https://www.dallasfed.org/) revealed that 11.4% said their institution or service provider had moved to limit customers’ AI agent activity on online banking platforms. AI Product.title: Wonder Unveils AI-Powered Restaurant Builder as Marc Lore Pushes Toward a Fully Automated Food Business
AI Product.titleZh: Wonder Unveils AI-Powered Restaurant Builder as Marc Lore Pushes Toward a Fully Automated Food Business
AI Product.content: # Wonder Unveils AI-Powered Restaurant Builder as Marc Lore Pushes Toward a Fully Automated Food Business Marc Lore’s food-tech startup Wonder unveiled a tool that uses AI to create restaurant concepts, menus, recipes, branding, and marketing materials. The launch comes days after the company disclosed it had confidentially filed paperwork to go public. BY JENNIFER CONRAD, SENIOR WRITER @JENNIFERCONRAD Marc Lore. Illustration: Inc.; Photos: Courtesy Wonder Marc Lore clearly doesn’t believe the “slop-bowl apocalypse” is upon us. His multi-restaurant food-delivery platform Wonder, which recently filed confidential paperwork to go public, today unveiled its AI-powered restaurant creation tool Wonder Create. It’s an early step in what he sees as a fully autonomous, robot-powered meal development, preparation, and delivery service. Wonder’s core business is a chain of about 170 ghost kitchens that offer delivery and takeout meals from multiple restaurants, including those Wonder incubated in house, developed with well-known chefs, or acquired. The idea is that diners can choose from multiple “restaurants” in a single order, with all of the food prepared and delivered out of a single location. With Wonder Create, the company is taking that concept even further, allowing people to build their own virtual restaurants with meals that can be ordered on Wonder. The platform’s AI tools will develop the name, logo, concept, photography, and product descriptions. The AI will also develop the recipes for any dish that can be made in Wonder’s specialized bowl-making machines using a set of 130 ingredients. It costs $10 a month to sign up, and the user determines the profit margin they want to make and takes a cut from each sale. ## Your own personal restaurant The first thing users can generate? Personalized bowls, salads, and poke bowls like those found at chains including Sweetgreen, Cava, and Chop’t, the latter of which is partnering with Wonder to trial new dishes and expand to new markets using Create. The daily digest for entrepreneurs and business leaders Lore says the platform will enable anyone to set up their own restaurant concepts in minutes. “You basically go in there and you say ‘build me a fast casual Mexican concept for Gen Z, for people who love World Cup’…and then you hit go,” Lore said, describing Wonder Create at a fireside chat with Inc. editor-in-chief Mike Hofman during the Inc. 5000 conference in October. Celebrities and athletes—including entrepreneur Gary Vaynerchuk, talk show host Andy Cohen, and the gymnast-turned-model Livvy Dunne—will have their own Wonder Create restaurants listed on the Wonder platform. Nonprofits such as the Ronald McDonald House New York and Food Bank for New York City will also have their own concepts on the platform, with the proceeds supporting their missions. Creators looking for new ways to make money from their followings can sign up, and the company says nearly 1,000 are already on the waitlist. But Lore says he expects that most users will be people with specialized diets, such as his own gluten-free, dairy-free, grain-free, high-protein diet. “These are the 20 menu items that I created for myself based on my dietary habits, my food preferences, my intolerances, the right micro macronutrients,” he says, describing how someone might build their concept. “It’s like the perfect restaurant for you.”

Infra & Chips.content: # As Trump and Xi meet, China's AI dreams face an unexpected hurdle: the Nvidia spy scandal ![](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20261110-133831-0053d0afea-web-3.28.0-4/grey-placeholder.png) ![Getty Images Jensen Huang, a Taiwanese-American man with grey hair and wearing a leather jacket, speaking on stage](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/21fe/live/6e3afdd0-deb6-11f1-8fb5-a771a656a227.jpg.webp) Jensen Huang is out but his shadow looms over the upcoming meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping this week. For Beijing, the former Nvidia CEO's dramatic fall is a major challenge - and not just because of claims that a Chinese spy may have honey-trapped Huang, one of the artificial intelligence industry's most influential figures. Rather, the allegations surrounding Huang and his affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang are turning into a new flashpoint in an already fragile US-China relationship. US intelligence reports claim she had ties to Beijing's intelligence apparatus - in particular the Ministry of State Security, China's main civilian spy agency. The claim remains unproven, but it has already reignited debate in Washington over exports of advanced chips to China and whether the Trump administration has been too willing to ease restrictions. For years now, advanced computer chips have been a key battleground in the US-China rivalry because they are essential for AI, supercomputing and military technology. Chinese officials are worried this scandal could strengthen voices in Washington who argue in favour of further limiting Chinese access to cutting-edge American tech. Just this week, the Trump administration introduced new export restrictions on Chinese firms that access advanced US chips in third countries such as Malaysia, Thailand or Brazil. They typically do this by renting computing power in data centres abroad to train their AI models. But some of the firms, like the one Alice Huang worked for, are also accused of smuggling chips to China, although they have denied this. Until now, this controversy appeared to be a sideshow in US-China relations. But with Beijing calling the new rules "economic coercion" on the eve of Trump arriving in Shenzhen, there is a growing risk it could become something much bigger. Democrats, who will control Congress come January, have made their position clear. Last Wednesday top Democrat Ted Lieu told Politico the Trump administration had been "1,000%" too deferential to Nvidia, putting national security at risk, while fellow Democrat Zoe Lofgren suggested Congress would now be more likely to restrict sales of AI chips to China. The BBC has approached the White House for comment. Beijing's foreign ministry had described the spy claims as a "smear against China". "The US should stop fabricating so-called espionage narratives to find pretexts for imposing technological blockades," spokesperson Mao Ning said last week. The ministry also seemed keen to keep the meeting on track, saying the two countries had kept "close communication regarding interactions between the two heads of state". ## Another 'spy balloon' incident? For the last year, Trump and Xi have been seeking to stabilise relations after a damaging tariff war that almost brought trade between the two countries to a standstill. The Trump administration's decision to [permit sales of advanced Nvidia H200 chips to China in late 2025](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ckg9q635q6po) was seen as evidence that both sides were searching for areas of co-operation, even while competition intensified. It was a rare move given Washington had spent years trying to limit China's access to the most advanced chips. Many in the US have long viewed these chips as a national security issue, arguing they could strengthen China's military and surveillance capabilities.
